subject: DYNAMIC LENGTH clause
notes: cite.py --check 13.18.19.4 "If the LIMIT phrase is not specified, the maximum number of characters that can be contained by the subject of the entry is implementor-defined." OK (GR2). Both halves verified: integer-1 is the maximum character count (MaxSizeOf = min(LIMIT, PREFIXED max, 0x3FFFFFDF)); probes: LIMIT 5 / LIMIT 3 / X(001) LIMIT 2 truncate MOVE "ABCDEFG" on the right to 5/3/2 characters; PIC N LIMIT 4 keeps 4 national CHARACTERS (not bytes). No LIMIT -> implementor maximum 1,073,741,791, documented as DOC-A.1-62 in docs/CONFORMANCE.md; a LIMIT above it warns COBOL2027 and clamps. Stale comment only: tests/conformance/2014/dynamic_length_limit.cob header calls the no-LIMIT item 'unbounded within the native string' - the bound is MaxLength; comment-level, not behavior. || Editions (adjudicator): 2014, 2023 (COBOL-2014 introduction per VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE; the 2023 Annex E lists only the 2023 SET enhancement for dynamic-length items, E.3 item 17)
